references.label: Only FE bypasses ordinary PWM feedback here

notes: Reviewed vendor definitions identify 3 as Battery Saver and 5 as Silent.
FE and FF are internal selectors; ordinary MCU mode commands reject values above 7.

A committed normal selector leaves FE and permits ordinary PWM feedback even while override bit 6 remains set. Automatic needs independent confirmation of normal manual state; no intermediate profile is required by this dispatch.

annotations.name: Fan 1 requested manual speed
annotations.description: Normal manual target before firmware clamping. This is neither actual rotation nor raw PWM duty.
notes: Below-minimum targets become zero only for selector 3 in the reviewed path; Silent selector 5 clamps to its minimum.

annotations.name: Manual fan flags
annotations.description: Normal manual-control state, separate from the thermal selector and override permission byte.
notes: Clearing direct-duty permission does not clear this manual-enable bit.
The SMBus receiver can stage a first bank-0 index-36 payload instead of storing it when the existing bit 7 is set. Mapped read-write access and bus completion alone do not prove the flag changed.

bits.name: Manual enable

annotations.name: Fan 2 direct-duty request

annotations.name: Override flags
annotations.description: Eight independent override bits. Bit 6 permits special fan duty and also holds one policy/event contributor.
notes: Mapped writes replace all eight bits; no masked or compare-and-swap operation is established.
Clearing bit 6 selects a saved power-dependent mode later, without immediately restoring PWM or Automatic.
No bounded independent cooling recovery after host failure is established.

bits.name: Other PWM override
bits.description: Uses bits in 0x80426 to drive three other PWM channels; external loads are unidentified.

bits.name: Input/state override A

bits.name: Input/state override B

bits.name: Peripheral policy bit

bits.name: Peripheral policy zero
bits.description: Under surrounding gates, forces peripheral-policy word 0x8023C to zero.

bits.name: Sensor update hold

bits.name: Special duty / policy hold
bits.description: Permits FE/FF and skips recomputation of contributor 0x80493; other contributors remain active.

bits.name: Policy candidate coupling

findings.title: Zero is ordinary at the PWM layer
findings.description: Normal firmware writes zero to the same actual PWM registers used by FE. This differs from a normal zero-RPM request and does not establish mechanical fan stop.

references.label: Zero is ordinary at the PWM layer

findings.title: Manual and automatic scales differ
findings.description: Manual target bytes use 100 RPM per count; automatic table targets use 50 RPM per count. Sensor bounds remain raw units.

findings.title: Factory tables are not live state
findings.description: The image contains four groups of factory thermal tables. Running firmware may load checked persistent tables; no live active table was read.

references.label: Factory tables are not live state

findings.title: Ordinary register mapping is not a write contract
findings.description: Transport reachability does not establish ownership, independent completion, thermal supervision or exact restoration.

references.label: Ordinary register mapping is not a write contract

findings.title: Surviving thermal responses do not establish cooling handback
findings.description: PROCHOT and high-sensor GPIO paths remain, but reviewed responses do not restart normal fans; stale sensor data and host-loss recovery remain unresolved.

references.label: Surviving thermal responses do not establish cooling handback

findings.title: Separate host mailbox selects its own bank
findings.description: The BRAM mailbox takes bank, index and count from F02290..92 and uses the common register map. It does not require changing the SMBus bank selector, unless the selected mapped operation itself writes that selector. Exact updater code uses host ports 300/301 for this path; no supported OpenBlade transport or exclusive field ownership follows.

references.label: Pinned updater metadata and host-port evidence

findings.title: Mailbox completion is not applied-state confirmation
findings.description: Status 80 is set before mapped processing. Read-only writes are skipped without changing it; writable fields receive whole-byte stores. The event wrapper clears the command afterward. This does not establish immutable requests, exclusive ownership, independent fan readback or a recovery lease.

findings.title: Legacy mailbox lifetime does not restore direct-duty cooling
findings.description: The updater method named Enable_Finite_Life_time corresponds to a guarded persistent-record write path, not an established volatile fan lease. A separate mailbox countdown clears legacy mailbox state; the FE direct-duty branch bypasses the ordinary fan countdown check. No host-loss cooling handback follows.

references.label: Copy record bytes and invoke persistent storage
FE branches before ordinary countdown check

findings.title: Silent Automatic requires seven-input hysteresis
findings.description: For the factory Silent curve, any enabled input at or above its current upper bound requests a rise; all seven must be strictly below their lower bounds to request a fall. Stage 1 lower bounds for channels 0,1,2,3,4,5,7 are 50,50,46,50,46,35,33. Equality prevents the fall. These are processed values, not interchangeable CPU/GPU Celsius thresholds.

findings.title: Stage dwell and PWM settling are separate
findings.description: Factory Silent stage-0/1 dwell limit 40 uses a strict counter comparison: the 42nd uninterrupted eligible evaluation selects the adjacent stage from a cleared count; its target is decoded later. Reload scans use a different initial selection. A zero target does not by itself prove sustained zero duty or stopped fans, because cadence, tach and cached duty state also participate.

references.label: Cached duty may replace the zero write

findings.title: Channel 7 strongly matches battery temperature
findings.description: Exact record 29A1C reads address byte 16, command 08 into word 8035C; FE60 converts it using (word - 2731) / 10 into channel 7. SBS command 08 reports pack temperature in tenths of Kelvin. This supports approximate degree-Celsius interpretation for channel 7 only; cached values and the unobserved live table remain relevant.

findings.title: Decoded zero targets can receive a 3000 RPM floor
findings.description: If either 80B08 or 80C08 equals one, the row decoder floors low targets at 3000 RPM. BRAM commands set/clear these flags; their additional effects include suppression of several sensor and peripheral paths. They are not fan-stop controls, and changing them does not establish a harmless or immediate policy transition.

findings.title: Legacy session timeout does not roll back persistent policy
findings.description: Legacy F0/F1 read storage; F3 prepares a write and admitted F4/F5 reach persistent writes. The Silent curve record 0x25 and auxiliary policy record 0x2D are distinct. The session countdown skips a conditional reload block while ordinary control remains reachable; expiry clears mailbox state without restoring old records, targets or PWM.

findings.title: An explicit normal selector can hand fans back from FE
findings.description: A committed Silent selector 5 leaves the FE branch and permits ordinary cadence-gated PWM feedback. Automatic also needs confirmed normal manual state. Another profile is not required, and idle Automatic may still request zero. The normal command leaves override permission and staged duty in place, so orderly fan handback is distinct from complete state restoration and host-loss recovery.
